children: Kosovo’s trade deficit widened to €568 million in August 2026, from €536.8 million in the same month a year earlier.
Imports rose 9% to €668.5 million, driven by a 6.6% increase in purchases from EU countries, mainly Germany, which accounted for 13.6% of total imports, followed by Italy (4.2%) and Poland (3.7%).
In contrast, imports from CEFTA countries (North Macedonia, Serbia and Albania) declined 2.1%.
The main imported products were machinery and transport equipment (23.2% of total), fuel (18.4%), processed goods (16.6%), and food and live animals (14.9%).

Meanwhile, exports surged 31.9% to €100.5 million, driven by a 29.8% increase in shipments to EU countries, particularly Germany, which accounted for 10.2% of total exports, followed by Italy (3.0%) and the Netherlands (2.2%).
Shipments to CEFTA countries (Albania, North Macedonia, Serbia and Montenegro) also rose 32.2%.
The main exported products were processed goods (25.4%), food and live animals (15.7%), and fuel (12.8%).

title: Kosovo Trade Deficit Widens in August
